exam: What study design best answers a question about the incidence of post‑surgical wound infection in a district hospital? — A prospective cohort because it follows patients over time and provides incidence data.
How would you adjust for HIV status when analysing risk factors for malaria in a cross‑sectional survey? — Include HIV as a covariate in multivariable logistic regression to control confounding.

A researcher plans a case‑control study but cannot locate a reliable control group. What alternative design could be used? — A retrospective cohort using existing hospital records, provided exposure data are recorded.

When sample size calculations show 350 participants are needed but only 200 can be recruited, what should you do? — Re‑calculate power, consider a larger effect size, or redesign as a pilot study with clear limitations.

Explain why a p‑value of 0.06 in a small trial of a new malaria prophylaxis may still be clinically important. — The study may be under‑powered; consider confidence intervals and effect size before dismissing the finding.
What ethical considerations are unique to research in low‑resource settings? — Obtain community consent, ensure benefit to the local population, and avoid exploitation of vulnerable participants.

Information bias – limited lab capacity leads to misclassification.
Confounding – HIV, malaria, and malnutrition often coexist.
sections.p: Bias, confounding, and resource constraints are the main threats to valid research in low‑resource hospitals.
